newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Additional support tests seen for dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Additional support tests seen for dlr/mark.

text.p: The dollar had edged higher against the mark by mid-afternoon on Friday, but chartists were calling for more consolidation and tests of key support in the early part of next week.

"I think we go down to the mid-1.67 area and that will be critical," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America. "I suspect that level will hold and the dollar will form a base and go higher but if we do get below that you're going to have a deeper correction."
Johnson said any bounce would probably hold between 1.6930 and 1.6950 where a number of intraday tops have been set.
Chartists said the market's reaction to the 1.6800/05 level, dollar/mark's lows on Friday and Wednesday, should give an early indication of where the rate is headed next week.

"We see support at today's low of 1.6805 out to 1.6750," said Rob Kepler, technical analyst at Lehman Brothers. "Those are the levels we have to break to activate better selling and if we get below there and the correction starts the extreme expected low next week is going to be 1.6670."
Kepler said more damage could lead dollar/mark down to 1.6550 and a secondary target at 1.6350, which he said represents a forty day exponential moving average.
In the longer-term, technicians said the dollar's trend against a host of other major currencies, including the mark, the Swiss franc and the yen, remains upward.
"Nothing goes straight up forever," said Johnson, explaining his rationale behind further dollar consolidation in the early part of next week.
"But the moving averages are all up, trendlines are all up and so you have to stay with it," he added.
